steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere. Shorter wavelengths of visible light (blue and violet) are scattered much more strongly than longer wavelengths (red and orange), spreading blue light in all directions across the sky. Although violet light is scattered even more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue and the sun emits slightly more blue than violet, so the sky ultimately looks blue to us.
